title: Minimax-Regret Randomized Treatment Rules with Categorical Instruments and Binary Outcomes
banked_reason: The promised Hruza-implementation comparison has been replaced by a generic randomized rectangle-oracle separation: the theorem does not establish that Hruza et al.'s deterministic learned rule has this oracle.
gap_reasons: The promised Hruza-implementation comparison has been replaced by a generic randomized rectangle-oracle separation: the theorem does not establish that Hruza et al.'s deterministic learned rule has this oracle, so either prove the workflow mapping under its stated scope or position the witness solely as a generic rectangle benchmark.
Removing the explicit Hruza target would substitute the promised kernel rather than repair it.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery built the finite response-type LP, exact three-action nonrectangular witness, separated-unique-face root-n theory, exact confidence-fiber coverage, and the face-intersection impossibility result, surviving multiple mathematical repairs. The run collapsed at D0.5 because those results compare randomized population joint and rectangle oracles, while the committed consumer promise targets Hruza et al.'s released deterministic learned rule. A future re-raise must add and verify the missing workflow, estimation, tie-breaking, surrogate, and optimization map; relabeling the result as a generic rectangle benchmark is not a faithful repair.
tldr: Randomized minimax regret under partial identification is not new: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye already analyze randomized statistical rules in a finite-sample Gaussian-likelihood decision problem.  For the binary-outcome, finite-stratum specialization of Song et al.'s model M1, this paper instead identifies the full categorical-instrument joint action-mean polytope and its complete population minimax correspondence.  The exact three-action witness has joint rule \(q^\dagger=(0,1/4,3/4)\) and value \(3/16\), whereas rectangularization selects \((0,0,1)\) with value \(1/4\); an exact rational matrix certifies all ten projected vertices, and uniform-response-type perturbations retain a value gap of at least \(1/32\) with full observed support.  On separated nondegenerate unique faces, the response bases and active saddle face are stable, but the observable table moves the active left-hand coefficient matrix; this yields the derivative \(-E H^{-1}(DH)u\) and a uniform root-\(n\) Gaussian policy-and-value law.  At the displayed codimension-one face intersection, class-uniform honest contraction fails at every vanishing rate absent separation, while the Bonferroni Clopper--Pearson confidence-fiber union retains exact correspondence containment and the deployed certificate uses verified primal and dual feasibility rather than a solver-reported gap.
gap: Random-linear-program limit theory fixes the constraint normals, while many-treatment statistical-rule theory studies repeated-sample decisions under point identification and existing partial-identification randomization formulas use binary marginal bounds. None gives fixed-law sampling inference for a categorical-instrument population mixture whose active regret normals change with the observed multinomial table.
fill: The paper states a nondegenerate unique-face margin class entirely in observable basis and KKT quantities, derives the moving-coefficient derivative and a uniform asymptotic linear representation, and proves a facet-normal obstruction to any fixed-matrix right-hand-side reduction. Exact set coverage and the three-action rectangle-oracle witness remain supporting consequences.
